check: correction: my earlier attribution of the tick-lag increase was wrong
earlierClaim: Comparing window A (08:47-11:00, no builds) at 22.5 lag events per hour against window B (11:00-11:45, while I ran builds) at 58.7, I concluded my builds roughly doubled the tick-lag rate, and recorded that as a measured boundary on what counts as non-interfering work.
betterEvidence: Per-refill segments, which the whole-window averages hid.

segments.note: cold start; the queue has just been filled and the server is warming
jumps immediately after the first refill, with no build running
the peak, still with no build running

correctedConclusion: Segments 1 through 4 ran with no build at all and already spanned 41.7 to 71.1 events per hour, so the elevated rate is the steady state after the first refill rather than something my builds caused. Segment 0's 5.6 is the cold start, and window A's 22.5 was that cold start averaged with the beginning of the steady state.
whatWasActuallyRight: The observation that watchers should avoid running runGameTest alongside the profile still stands on its own merits - it starts a second Minecraft server and competes for the same cores - but the specific doubling I claimed is not supported by the segmented data.
whyThisMatters: The earlier claim was recorded as a measured boundary, and a wrong measurement is worse than a conservative rule of thumb because it looks precise. A later reader comparing segment rates would have found the boundary contradicted by the data.
